instruction: Increase every italicized glossary term from 12 point to 14 point. Keep the terms italic, and preserve all surrounding text, colors, links, paragraph breaks, and remaining formatting.

states.value:
FIELD RESPONSE GLOSSARY
Community Cooling Center | Volunteer Desk Edition
Use this glossary when recording welfare checks, room conditions, and handovers during a heat response. Record the exact time, observed condition, and action taken.
MONITORING NOTES
At noon, the duty lead compares the shaded thermometer with the heat index before deciding whether outdoor queues need additional shade or shorter waiting periods.
Staff open an additional cooled room when the approved cooling threshold is reached, then check drinking-water supplies and notify facilities.
When the entrance queue grows, supervisors shorten the hydration interval for volunteers working in direct sun or moving supplies.
FIELD ACTIONS
Before a volunteer takes over the entrance desk, the outgoing worker completes a buddy check and identifies the nearest cooled recovery space.
Anyone who feels unwell moves to shaded recovery while the desk records the start time, water offered, observed condition, and next decision.
A sudden change in alertness, balance, or speech is an escalation trigger that stops routine duties and starts the response plan.
RETURN AND CLOSEOUT
No one returns to a warm work area until a supervisor completes the re-entry check and confirms the next scheduled break.
At the end of the shift, the duty lead signs the closeout log after checking room temperatures, supply levels, unresolved concerns, and equipment faults.
REFERENCE DESK
Current procedures are available at https://safety.cooling-center.example/field-guide. Report corrections to glossary@cooling-center.example.
REMINDER
Record observable facts and exact times; do not invent a diagnosis or copy an earlier note.
Edition 3.1 • Prepared for summer drills • Review after every activation
